authors: Ji M, Greening C, Vanwonterghem I, et al.
title: Atmospheric trace gases support primary production in Antarctic desert surface soil
one_line_key_finding: Atmospheric H2 and CO scavenging sustains chemosynthetic primary production in Antarctic surface soil communities.

authors: Bay SK, Dong X, Bradley JA, et al.
title: Trace gas oxidizers are widespread and active members of soil microbial communities
one_line_key_finding: Over 70% of soil bacterial taxa across 19 phyla encode enzymes to consume H2/CO as supplemental electron donors.

authors: Ortiz M, Leung PM, Shelley G, et al.
title: Multiple energy sources and metabolic strategies sustain microbial diversity in Antarctic desert soils
one_line_key_finding: Trace-gas oxidation and chemolithotrophy, not photosynthesis, are the dominant energy strategies sustaining Antarctic soil microbial diversity.

authors: Leung PM, Bay SK, Meier DV, et al.
title: Energetic basis of microbial growth and persistence in desert ecosystems
one_line_key_finding: Reviews how dormancy and trace-gas scavenging underpin microbial persistence under desert carbon/water limitation.

authors: Ray AE, Zaugg J, Benaud N, Chelliah DS, Bay S, Wong HL, Leung PM, Ji M, Terauds A, Montgomery K, Greening C, Cowan DA, Kong W, Williams TJ, Hugenholtz P, Ferrari BC
title: Atmospheric chemosynthesis is phylogenetically and geographically widespread and contributes significantly to carbon fixation throughout cold deserts
one_line_key_finding: Atmospheric chemosynthesis is a globally distributed process across cold deserts contributing significantly to carbon fixation.

authors: Hutchinson TF, Holland SIR, Clarke DA, et al. (Greening C)
title: Resilient Antarctic soil bacteria consume trace gases across wide temperature ranges
one_line_key_finding: H2 consumption is thermally resilient (-20 to +75C); CO and CH4 oxidation occur over wider temperature ranges than expected.

authors: Thompson AR, Adams BJ, Hogg ID, Yooseph S
title: Evidence for trace gas metabolism and widespread antibiotic synthesis in an abiotically-driven, Antarctic soil ecosystem
one_line_key_finding: Many McMurdo Dry Valley bacteria perform trace gas metabolism, with widespread antibiotic biosynthesis/resistance genes.

authors: Bay SK, Dong X, Bradley JA, Leung PM, et al.
title: Soil microbiomes with the genetic capacity for atmospheric chemosynthesis are widespread across the poles and are associated with moisture, carbon, and nitrogen limitation
one_line_key_finding: hhyL/rbcL1E genes for atmospheric H2-driven chemosynthesis are widespread in polar/high-altitude cold-desert soils, linked to moisture/C/N limitation.

authors: Lynch RC, Darcy JL, Kane NC, Nemergut DR, Schmidt SK
title: Metagenomic evidence for metabolism of trace atmospheric gases by high-elevation desert Actinobacteria
one_line_key_finding: Sparse Actinobacteria-dominated communities encode H2/CO oxidation genes, suggesting trace-gas chemoautotrophy fuels low-energy high-altitude desert soils.

authors: Jordaan K, Lappan R, Dong X, Aitkenhead IJ, Bay SK, Chiri E, et al.
title: Hydrogen-oxidizing bacteria are abundant in desert soils and strongly stimulated by hydration
one_line_key_finding: Group 1h/1l [NiFe]-hydrogenases, FDH and CODH are among the most expressed genes; mixotrophy via trace-gas oxidation underpins desert survival, boosted by hydration.

authors: Cordero PRF, Bayly K, Leung PM, Huang C, Islam ZF, Schittenhelm RB, et al.
title: Atmospheric carbon monoxide oxidation is a widespread mechanism supporting microbial survival
one_line_key_finding: Form I Mo-Cu CO dehydrogenase lets bacteria respire sub-atmospheric CO as a supplemental energy source during carbon starvation; ancient, widespread trait.

authors: Schulze-Makuch D, Wagner D, Kounaves SP, Mangelsdorf K, et al.
title: Transitory microbial habitat in the hyperarid Atacama Desert
one_line_key_finding: Indigenous microbes are present and episodically active after rare rain events; biomolecular and replication evidence of transient activity in the driest soils.

authors: (review)
title: Inside the Atacama Desert: uncovering the living microbiome of an extreme environment
one_line_key_finding: Review of the active Atacama microbiome, including survival strategies and trace-gas/chemoautotrophic metabolism in the hyperarid core.

authors: Ray AE, Tribbia DZ, Cowan DA, Ferrari BC
title: Clearing the air: unraveling past and guiding future research in atmospheric chemosynthesis
one_line_key_finding: Review of atmospheric chemosynthesis (high-affinity H2/CO/CH4 oxidation <=ppbv); synthesizes desert evidence and frames open questions for the field.

authors: Greening C, Biswas A, Carere CR, Jackson CJ, Taylor MC, Stott MB, Cook GM, Morales SE
title: Genomic and metagenomic surveys of hydrogenase distribution indicate H2 is a widely utilised energy source for microbial growth and survival
one_line_key_finding: Hydrogenases are taxonomically widespread across 51 phyla; H2 oxidation is a near-universal strategy for microbial energy generation, growth and persistence.

authors: Sondergaard D, Pedersen CNS, Greening C
title: HydDB: a web tool for hydrogenase classification and analysis
one_line_key_finding: Defines an expanded 38-class hydrogenase taxonomy and provides a kNN+CDD web tool for rapid functional classification of hydrogenase sequences.

authors: Greening C, Carere CR, Rushton-Green R, Harold LK, Hards K, Taylor MC, Morales SE, Stott MB, Cook GM
title: Persistence of the dominant soil phylum Acidobacteria by trace gas scavenging
one_line_key_finding: Energy-starved Pyrinomonas (Acidobacteria) persists by scavenging atmospheric trace H2 via high-affinity hydrogenase, a general survival mechanism for dominant soil phyla.

authors: Liot Q, Constant P
title: Breathing air to save energy: new insights into the ecophysiological role of high-affinity [NiFe]-hydrogenase in Streptomyces avermitilis
one_line_key_finding: Streptomyces avermitilis high-affinity [NiFe]-hydrogenase enables atmospheric H2 oxidation in spores/dormant cells, supporting energy conservation during starvation.

authors: Grinter R, Kropp A, Venugopal H, Senger M, Badley J, Cabotaje PR, et al.
title: Structural basis for bacterial energy extraction from atmospheric hydrogen
one_line_key_finding: Cryo-EM structure of Mycobacterium smegmatis Huc shows hydrophobic gas channels selecting atmospheric H2 over O2, making trace-H2 oxidation energetically feasible.

authors: King GM, Weber CF
title: Distribution, diversity and ecology of aerobic CO-oxidizing bacteria
one_line_key_finding: Reviews globally distributed aerobic CO-oxidizing bacteria and cox/CODH genes; CO oxidation is a widespread, biogeochemically important trait (OA substitute: Cordero 2019).

authors: Greening C, Grinter R
title: Microbial oxidation of atmospheric trace gases
one_line_key_finding: Synthesizes how diverse aerobic bacteria oxidize atmospheric H2, CO and CH4 for growth/survival, with ecological, biogeochemical and astrobiological significance.

authors: Conrad R
title: Soil microorganisms as controllers of atmospheric trace gases (H2, CO, CH4, OCS, N2O, and NO)
one_line_key_finding: Soils are the dominant biological sink controlling atmospheric H2, CO, CH4, OCS, N2O and NO via the microbial production/consumption balance.

authors: Ehhalt DH, Rohrer F
title: The tropospheric cycle of H2: a critical review
one_line_key_finding: Critical review of the global tropospheric H2 budget; soil uptake (~60-80 Tg/yr) is the dominant sink, larger and more uncertain than photochemical loss.

authors: Paulot F, Paynter D, Naik V, Malyshev S, Menzel R, Horowitz LW
title: Global modeling of hydrogen using GFDL-AM4.1: sensitivity of soil removal and radiative forcing
one_line_key_finding: GFDL-AM4.1 best reproduces surface H2 when soil deposition velocity is modulated by soil moisture, temperature and soil carbon; soil removal is the dominant sink governing H2 radiative forcing.

authors: Ocko IB, Hamburg SP
title: Climate consequences of hydrogen emissions
one_line_key_finding: Hydrogen is a potent indirect greenhouse gas; leakage along the hydrogen value chain can substantially offset the climate benefits of switching from fossil fuels.

authors: Bertagni MB, Pacala SW, Paulot F, Porporato A
title: Risk of the hydrogen economy for atmospheric methane
one_line_key_finding: H2 leakage extends atmospheric CH4 lifetime by competing for OH radicals; the soil H2 sink is a key uncertain control on the net climate impact of a hydrogen economy.

authors: Buzzard V, Thorne D, Gil-Loaiza J, Cueva A, Meredith LK
title: Sensitivity of soil hydrogen uptake to natural and managed moisture dynamics in a semiarid urban ecosystem
one_line_key_finding: Soil moisture dynamics strongly modulate the atmospheric-H2 soil sink in semiarid systems, with uptake peaking at intermediate moisture and suppressed when dry or saturated.

authors: Tveit AT, Hestnes AG, Robinson SL, Schintlmeister A, Dedysh SN, Jehmlich N, et al.
title: Widespread soil bacterium that oxidizes atmospheric methane
one_line_key_finding: Isolated USCalpha Methylocapsa gorgona grows on air-level CH4 plus H2/CO, demonstrating high-affinity atmospheric methane oxidation as a real growth-supporting metabolism.
